target.name: Epsilon Indi B
target.summary_plain: Two brown dwarfs, objects too massive to be planets but too small to shine like stars, circling each other about 12 light-years away. Together they orbit the star Epsilon Indi A from roughly 1,500 times the Earth-Sun distance.

astrometry.source: Gaia DR3 6412596012146801152 (Ba+Bb photocentre; RV assumed equal to eps Ind A)

render.note: One asinh stretch per detector (0.5-99.7 percentiles of all its epochs), shared by every epoch, so brightness changes between frames are real. Co-adds: IMAGE minus ZODI, official photometry mask 0x3C028E44 rejected, OVERFLOW kept and flagged, then an inverse-variance mean after 3-sigma clipping (drops single-exposure streaks). Then vs Now: each image stretched by its own 0.5-99.7 percentiles. Differences: S/N, linear between the limits.

motion.method: Per-exposure ePSF position fits (D1-D6, S/N >= 10, 100 mas floor); sigma-clipped linear fit with parallax removed
motion.verdict_text: SPHEREx measures 4.70 ± 0.02″ per year toward PA 122°; Gaia DR3 predicts 4.69″ per year toward PA 122°: the speed agrees within 0.3%. Between Oct 2025 and Sep 2026 it moved 4.6″, as predicted to within 0.3%. The direction agrees within 0.3°.

notes: Each point is one exposure: forced photometry at the catalogue position (ePSF fit, or a fit to the PSF wings when the core is saturated).
Saturated points are shown hollow and excluded from fits.
2 of 459 points are saturated (OVERFLOW in the core).
The quick-look curve is the Year-1 spectral cube at 12.9″ pixels: it blends close neighbours, and channels where the star saturates are left empty.

checks.name: all detectors proper motion total within 5% of catalog
all detectors proper-motion PA within 3 deg
per-exposure position scatter < 0.5 arcsec (radial RMS of residuals)

warnings: Saturated (OVERFLOW) in 2 of 459 exposures. Saturated pixels are kept in the images and outlined in the flags overlay; their brightness comes from fits to the PSF wings.
Epsilon Indi Ba and Bb (about 0.7″ apart) are unresolved: SPHEREx measures their combined light and photocentre.

The bright star Epsilon Indi A lies just beyond the right (west) edge: its glow, and probably the ring-shaped ghost north of the target, show in the long-wavelength frames. The October 2025 D5 and D6 co-adds also show a faint streak running south-east from the target that appears in no other epoch: an unflagged artefact or a faint moving object, not the brown dwarfs.
2 of 4 epochs are partial (fewer than 12 images per detector): shown greyed out.
False colour exists for 3 of 4 epochs: it needs D1, D3 and D6 in the same epoch.
